newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African labour dispute body hears 10,000th case.
newsitem.headline: S.African labour dispute body hears 10,000th case.

text.p: South Africa's Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA), heard its 10,000th case in the Gauteng region on Wednesday since opening its doors in November, senior commissioner Gavin Hartford said.

The Gauteng region, which as the industrial heartland of the country handles the bulk of the commission's case load, boasts a 68-percent settlement rate in conciliated cases, Hartford told a news briefing.

Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said last month the CCMA had achieved an 86-percent success rate nationally since it was set up in terms of the new Labour Relations Act (LRA) to provide quick and fair mediation in labour disputes.
The new LRA came into effect in November 1996.
"Under the old Labour Relations Act, the settlement rate was very low, varying between nought and 30 percent. A 68-percent settlement rate is high by world standards, " Hartford said.
Under the old act, disputes that could not be settled were referred to the Industrial Court and often took a year or more to be heard.

Hartford said most cases in Gauteng involved workers in the commercial distribution sector. Other main sectors were domestic workers, private security firms, the food and beverage sector, building and construction and banking.
He said the farming sector had hardly featured because there was not sufficient knowledge about the services provided.
"People in the urban areas are first to make use of the service," he said.

A major challenge for the dispute body was to provide efficient service to the public to ensure disputes were timely heard. Another was to sustain a high quality of settlements within the commission, he added.
